claim: For the canonical Newton–Leipnik flow \(\dot x=-\tfrac25x+y+10yz,\ \dot y=-x-\tfrac25y+5xz,\ \dot z=\alpha z-5xy\), the parameter sign gives an exact compact-recurrence trichotomy. If \(\alpha<0\), the origin is the only bounded complete orbit and supports the only compact invariant probability measure; if \(\alpha=0\), compact invariant probability measures are exactly the compactly supported probabilities on the equilibrium \(z\)-axis. If \(\alpha>0\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies \(\mathbb E_\mu[xy\mid z]=\alpha z/5\), \(\mathbb E_\mu[(z+1/20)^2]=1/400+\mathbb E_\mu[x^2]/(5\alpha)\), and \(\mathbb E_\mu[(z-1/10)^2]=1/100+2\mathbb E_\mu[y^2]/(5\alpha)\). Equality in either centered-square lower bound holds only for the origin measure. Consequently every other compact stationary state gives positive mass outside both slabs \(-1/10\le z\le0\) and \(0\le z\le1/5\); a nonconstant periodic orbit that stays in \(z\ge0\) reaches \(z>1/5\), while one that stays in \(z\le0\) reaches \(z<-1/10\).

correctness.rationale: The theorem follows from four exact Lie-derivative identities. The negative-parameter case uses a coercive quadratic Lyapunov function with explicit exponential decay; the zero-parameter classification follows from its stationary balance; the positive-parameter conditional and square-defect laws follow from invariant-measure generator identities. Equality rigidity was checked on the invariant support under the actual vector field. The included exact-rational checker replayed the polynomial identities and returned VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: The result gives a single rigorous structural description across all signs of the feedback parameter, whereas the inspected Newton–Leipnik literature is dominated by numerical attractor geometry, bifurcation models and control. For positive parameter it constrains every compact stationary state—not just a simulated attractor—through a conditional law and two sharp centered-square defects, yielding immediate recurrence-height barriers. The constants are exact and the baseline bounds are sharp because the origin is invariant, while every non-origin compact stationary state is strictly separated.
